candidates.statement: This guidance is intended for sponsor-investigators 2 (hereafter referred to as sponsors) 18 developing individualized investigational antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) drug products for a 19 severely debilitating or life-threatening (SDLT) genetic disease. 3 Most often, individuals with 20 such diseases will have no alternative treatment options, and their diseases will be rapidly 21 progressing, resulting in early death and/or devastating or irreversible morbidity within a short 22 time frame without treatment. In these situations, drug development targeted to a larger number 23 of patients with the same disease is not anticipated because of the specificity of the mechanism 24 of action of the ASO combined with the rarity of the treatment-amenable patient population. The 25 gene variant or variants that are targeted by the ASO drug product should be unique to the trial 26 participant(s) and generally only reported in a small number of patients (typically 1 to 2) in the 27 disease population. If more than a few patients may be candidates for targeted treatment with the 28 ASO drug product, then the ASO is no longer considered individualized, and the sponsor should 29 discuss a drug development plan of the investigational ASO drug product for a larger patient 30 population with the relevant review division. 31
candidates.context: The focus of this guidance is to describe important clinical considerations for investigational new 33 drug application (IND) submissions to support initial and continued administration, dosing, and 34 clinical monitoring of an individual with a SDLT disease attributable to a unique genetic 35

candidates.statement: variant(s) that may be amenable to an ASO drug product. The individualized ASO drug product 36 should belong to a well-characterized chemical class 4 (i.e., a chemical class for which there is 37 substantial nonclinical information and clinical experience that is either publicly available or to 38 which the sponsor has right of reference). 39
candidates.context: 3 Severely debilitating means diseases or conditions that cause major irreversible morbidity. Life-threatening means diseases or conditions where the likelihood of death is high unless the course of the disease is interrupted and those with potentially fatal outcomes, where the endpoint of clinical trial analysis is survival (see 21 CFR 312.81). This guidance does not address clinical and regulatory considerations for the development of an 41 individualized ASO drug product for commercial marketing. This guidance also does not address 42 the nonclinical data 5 or the drug product quality requirements 6 to initiate administration of an 43 individualized ASO drug product in humans, or the administrative and procedural 44 recommendations for an IND submission. 7

candidates.statement: Under FDA regulations, a protocol under which an individual ASO drug product is administered 74 to a human subject must be reviewed and approved by an institutional review board (IRB) before 75 it is allowed to proceed (21 CFR part 56). If children 9 are to be included in the protocol, the 76 requirements in 21 CFR part 50, subpart D ( Additional Safeguards for Children in Clinical 77 Investigations) also must be met. Similarly, in accordance with 21 CFR 50.20, the sponsor must 78 obtain legally effective informed consent from the trial participant, or the participant’s legally 79 authorized representative, before administration of the investigational ASO drug product. The 80 informed consent must include all the required basic elements under 21 CFR 50.25(a), including, 81 but not limited to, a description of reasonably foreseeable risks or discomforts to the trial 82 participant and any potential benefits which may reasonably be expected from the investigational 83 ASO drug product. When appropriate, significant new findings developed during the course of 84 the research that might have implications for the trial participant’s willingness to continue in the 85 research should be provided to the participant (and/or the participant’s legally authorized 86 representative). In addition, the sponsor should discuss with the applicable IRB how and when 87 significant new findings will be provided to the trial participant. 10

candidates.statement: Sponsors should consider the following recommendations for dosing of investigational ASO 115 drug products and include all relevant information in the IND submission: 116
candidates.context: C. Dosing Considerations 113 • The starting dose should be based on available nonclinical data and be scientifically 118 supported by available information from other ASO drug products in the chemical class 119 and/or prior clinical experience. In general, the starting dose should be expected to have a 120 pharmacologic effect, based on available nonclinical in vitro and/or in vivo data. 11

If a loading dose or doses are proposed, the protocol 131 should contain a rationale for using a loading dose(s) and maintenance dose interval(s) 132 based on considerations such as the ASO drug product’s half-life, likely distribution (e.g., 133 target areas in the central nervous system (CNS), kidney), and anticipated toxicities with 134 different doses. 135

candidates.context: D. Drug Product Administration Procedures 149 • Sponsors should administer the starting dose and each escalation in dose in an inpatient 154 (hospital) setting. candidates.statement: Sponsors should consider the following recommendations for safety assessments of 172 investigational ASO drug products and detail all safety procedures and assessments in the IND 173 submission: 174
candidates.context: • Sponsors should perform routine safety assessments (e.g., adverse events, vital signs, 176 electrocardiogram, laboratory assessments) while the investigational ASO drug product is 177 being administered and for a period after stopping administration based on the anticipated 178 half-life of the ASO drug product. Safety monitoring should be informed by nonclinical 179 toxicology findings, potential off-target gene knockdown effects predicted by 180 bioinformatic tools, and previously identified safety risks associated with the use of other 181 ASO drug products of the same chemical class. The protocol should include a detailed 182 schedule of safety assessments. 183

Assessment of Clinical Response 210

candidates.statement: Sponsors should consider the following recommendations for assessing participants’ clinical 212 response to investigational ASO drug products and outline in the IND submission a plan for 213 evaluation of clinical benefit in relation to observed toxicities (as applicable): 214
candidates.context: F. Assessment of Clinical Response 210 • The assessment of whether the ASO drug product is providing clinical benefit to the 216 participant is an important element of the overall clinical assessment throughout the 217 administration period. To best inform decisions regarding continuation of administration, 218 sponsors should carefully track clinical changes over time with a specific plan for 219 adjustment of the dosing regimen to achieve a desirable clinical response. The protocol 220 should clearly outline the specific method(s) and timing of clinical assessments. 221
